MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

PATIENT: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
SPECIMEN: Peripheral blood
COLLECTION DATE: [redacted date]
REPORT DATE: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Suspected fragile X syndrome

TEST PERFORMED
FRAXA Expansion Mutation Analysis by PCR

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. PCR amplification of the FMR1 gene CGG repeat region was performed using fluorescently labeled primers. Fragment analysis was conducted by capillary electrophoresis to determine CGG repeat number.

RESULTS
FMR1 Gene (FRAXA locus): Normal sized allele detected
CGG Repeat Number: Within normal range (<55 repeats)

INTERPRETATION
This patient has a normal sized allele at the FRAXA locus. Based on these findings, the patient is unlikely to be affected with fragile X syndrome. Normal alleles contain fewer than 55 CGG repeats and are stably transmitted to offspring.

This test detects expansions in the FMR1 gene associated with fragile X syndrome. Full mutations (>200 repeats) cause fragile X syndrome, while premutations (55-200 repeats) are associated with fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS) and fragile X-associated primary ovarian insufficiency (FXPOI).

LIMITATIONS
This assay may not detect all genetic causes of intellectual disability or autism spectrum disorder. Rare variants outside the CGG repeat region are not assessed by this test.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
